title: postloop-notes-gestalt-evaluation-tereza-kovacs
content:
Candidate: Tereza Kovacs
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving)
Interviewer / note-taker: Hector Alvarez
Panel: Maya Chang, Diego Ramos, Fiona Liu
Interview date: 2026-03-09

1) One-sentence gestalt
Tereza is a pragmatic engineer with strong production instincts around latency-cost tradeoffs and KV cache strategies; she showed solid system-level thinking but few signal flags on leadership or cross-team negotiation at this level. Recommend: proceed to take-home + manager loop before final.

2) Quick pros/cons (bulleted)
Pros:
- Deep practical experience optimizing token-level latency for generation workloads (examples below).
- Clear mental model of KV cache, prefix caching, and batching interactions.
- Thoughtful about rollout safety (canary->traffic-shift->fallback).
- Communicates tradeoffs concisely; good at enumerating failure modes.

Cons / unknowns:
- Limited visible ownership of a major product rollout (she shipped infra components but not end-to-end product).
- Surface-level familiarity with quantization options; theoretical knowledge but fewer hands-on experiments.
- Soft-skill signal: tends to default to technical framing rather than stakeholder framing in behavioral answers.

3) System design deep dive (30m)
Prompt: Design a low-latency multi-tenant inference runner that supports model variants, per-tenant routing policies, and transparent fallback to cheaper quantized variants.
Notes:
- Started with an explicit request flow: request -> policy router -> placement decision -> runner pod -> KV cache lookup -> generation -> postprocess. Good baseline.
- Emphasized separation of policy layer (routing) from runtime; suggested policy as "declarative rules + priority queue". Good for observability.
- Proposed hybrid cache: hot-prefix in RAM local to runner, cold-prefix on shared redis with async prefetch. Discussed consistency and TTL decisions. Practical and implementable.
- Batch sizing strategy: recommended dynamic batching by latency budget per tenant and token horizon; suggested circuit-breaker to throttle heavy tails.
- Fallbacks: proposed automated graceful degradation: quantized variant -> smaller context windows -> sampling/truncation. Stressed metrics to monitor (user-perceived latency, top-k token loss, regression alerts).
- Missed opportunity: did not propose autoscaling policy that ties directly to model-specific KV cache hit-rate (we discussed after and she agreed it’s an important knob).

4) Coding / whiteboard (30m)
Exercise: implement a simplified token-eviction policy for a prefix-KV cache that balances recency and model-affinity.
Notes:
- Wrote clear pseudocode for an LRU+weight scheme where entries have affinity score based on model id and prefix frequency.
- Complexity analysis: correctly identified O(1) ops for get/put using linked hashmap + heap for affinity adjustments.
- Edge cases: handled race windows and eviction under concurrent writes in a sketchy but sensible way.
- Follow-up question: how to test under distributed runners? She sketched a test harness simulating cross-node cache misses and convergence — good practical thinking.

5) Behavioral / culture fit
- Examples of collaboration: discussed driving a cadence with SRE and product to reduce 95th %-ile latency. Showed empathy for product tradeoffs but rarely framed wins in terms of customer impact (tends to focus on technical metrics).
- Conflict story: described a time disagreement with a PM about rollout speed; she highlighted data-driven persuasion and falling back to flags. Not dramatic but consistent with our culture.

6) Level calibration + comparators
- Senior IC at Redwood (IC3/IC4 depending on expectations): technical depth fits strong Senior; for Staff would need broader ownership and cross-team influence examples.
- Compared to recent hires: stronger systems instincts than candidate X (infra hire 2025) but less product-leading experience than candidate Y (runtime lead).

7) Red flags worth noting
- No major safety/secure-by-design examples (encryption of KV, key rotation, tenant-level data separation) — we probed and she has familiarity but not strong hands-on.
- Limited direct experience with quantization tooling (Q8/Q4 experiments). Could be a ramp area.

8) Rubric scores (0-5; subjective)
- System design: "4"
- Coding & correctness: "4"
- Performance-oriented intuition (latency/cost): "4"
- Product/ stakeholder orientation: "3"
- Ownership & cross-team impact: "3"
- Communication: "4"
- Overall recommendation: "proceed to manager loop + take-home"

9) Suggested take-home and manager loop focus
- Take-home: small lab where candidate must profile a toy transformer serving loop, implement two cache policies, and show token-latency/cost tradeoffs with short write-up. Timebox 6 hours. Focus areas: measurable latency, test harness, reproducibility.
- Manager loop: focus on examples of shipping cross-functional projects, prioritization tradeoffs, and stakeholder influence. Also probe production security / tenant isolation designs deeper.

10) Next steps / possible outcomes
- If take-home shows practical experiments and clear metrics -> move to offer at Senior IC (IC4) level.
- If take-home is mixed (good engineering but limited production breadth) -> consider offer with mentorship track or second manager-led project interview.
- If take-home is weak -> close.

11) Private notes (personal heuristics)
- I was impressed by her ability to move from abstractions to concrete levers quickly. That maps well to our immediate infra needs (prefix cache wins).
- Concern: onboarding to our quantization + compliance reqs might take 3-4 months; plan to pair with an applied-ml engineer if hired.

Timestamped short log:
- 2026-03-09 10:05 — intro/behavioral (clean)
- 2026-03-09 10:25 — system design (strong)
- 2026-03-09 11:00 — coding sketch (clear)
- 2026-03-09 11:30 — wrap, questions (good)

Summary line for panel vote: "Technical match for Senior runtime role; recommend take-home to validate production quantization and tenant-security exposure; likely a strong contributor to latency/cost SLO work."

Action items (owner tags):
- Maya: draft take-home test + grading rubric (due 2026-03-13)
- Diego: prepare manager-loop question list around security/tenancy (due 2026-03-14)
- Hector: follow up with candidate scheduling for take-home (email sent)

End of note.
